check_file.description: Path to a single file to parse in isolation (instead of running as LSP server). Overrides other settings.

compile_commands_dir.description: Path to directory containing compile_commands.json. clangd searches parent paths if invalid.

background_index.description: Build and persist background index on disk.

removed.description: Glob patterns for compiler drivers that clangd may safely execute (e.g., '/usr/bin/**/clang-*'). Each glob is matched against the driver basename or full path.

path_mappings.description: List of client/server path mappings. Each entry is of form 'client_path=server_path'. First match wins for a given file path.

enable_config.description: Enable loading user and project YAML config (always effective in config files).

log.description:
Log verbosity: 'error', 'info', or 'verbose'. Logs written to stderr. Note: The man page lists 'error', 'info', 'verbose'. The schema had 'error' as default, which matches the 'error' option description 'Error messages only'. However, clangd's actual default log level is 'info'. Let's check the man page: `--log=<value> ... =error - Error messages only ... =info - High level execution tracing`. It doesn't specify a default. Clangd defaults to 'info'. The schema had 'error'. This is likely a factual error. Let's fix it to 'info'.
    },

pch_storage.description:
Where to store precompiled headers: 'memory' (faster, higher memory) or 'disk' (persistent).
    },

malloc_trim.description:
Enable periodic memory release via malloc_trim(3).
    },

workers.description:
Number of async worker threads (background index shares pool). 0 means default (CPU-dependent).
    }
